cvEn:
Efraim Mizrahi, son of Frida and Eliyahu, was born on 28 Cheshvan 5690 (1 December 1929) in Jerusalem. In his city he completed elementary school and began work as a trainee in the broadcasting service. While still a boy he joined the Betar movement (the Yehuda platoon) and later the Irgun underground.

When news arrived from Lake Success of the partition decision of 29 November 1947 and the establishment of the Jewish state, the boy Efraim joined the dancers in Zion Square and danced with enthusiasm. Remembering that Jerusalem had been placed outside the borders of the Jewish state, he told his friend that he was prepared to give his life for the integrity of the homeland. The next day the Jewish neighborhoods were already fighting for their existence, but Efraim went out to fight specifically in the Old City. There the boy fought with extraordinary courage, as an experienced adult soldier with a Sten gun, against the enemy's heavy weapons, until he fell in battle on 10 Iyar 5708 (19 May 1948). He was buried in a mass grave in the Old City of Jerusalem.

His name is inscribed on the monument erected in the military cemetery on Mount Herzl in memory of the fallen of the Jewish Quarter, and in memory of the fighters who fell in the battle for Jerusalem and were buried on the Mount of Olives.
